newsitem.title: USA: Crews work to refloat grounded VGO tanker in Texas.
newsitem.headline: Crews work to refloat grounded VGO tanker in Texas.

text.p: Barge crews on Friday continued lightering a cargo of vacuum gasoil (VGO) from the tanker Overseas Valdez, which grounded on Thursday about five miles off the coast of Galveston Island, a U.S. Coast Guard spokesman said.

About 50,000 barrels of the ship's cargo of 274,000 barrels of the heavy residual fuel oil were lightered onto barges overnight, and the Coast Guard expected the ship to be refloated as a high tide rolled in about midday, the spokesman said.
"It will probably be another four to six hours, probably around noon when the tide rolls in," Coast Guard Petty Officer Travis Inmon told Reuters.
There was no leakage from the ship, which is owned by Maritime Overseas Corp of New York and sailed from a Texas City refinery, the Coast Guard said. Its destination was not immediately available.
The tanker apparently snared a buoy line in its rudder while passing an inbound ship, losing steering control and grounding near the mouth of the Houston Ship Channel, Coast Guard officials said.
Shipping traffic in the ship channel, a waterway connecting Houston's port and refinery row to the Gulf of Mexico, was not affected, the Coast Guard said.
